title: Bar Classics: Food & Drink
description: Four rounds and a final wager spanning spirits, cellar lore, kitchen science, and famous food moments.

questions.prompt: A classic margarita is built on which spirit?
questions.answer_note: source: IBA official cocktail list — the margarita is tequila, triple sec, and lime juice.

questions.prompt: Guinness has been brewed at St. James's Gate in which city since 1759?
questions.answer_note: source: Guinness archives — Arthur Guinness leased the St. James's Gate brewery in Dublin in 1759.

questions.prompt: Botanically speaking, peanuts are true nuts.
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — peanuts are legumes in the pea family, not botanical nuts.

questions.prompt: A classic Mojito is built on which spirit?
questions.answer_note: source: IBA official cocktail list — the Mojito is white rum, lime, mint, sugar, and soda.

questions.prompt: Which fresh herb is the base of classic Genoese pesto?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — pesto alla genovese is pounded basil with pine nuts, garlic, cheese, and olive oil.

questions.prompt: The Scoville scale rates what quality in peppers?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Wilbur Scoville's 1912 scale measures chili pepper pungency from capsaicin.

questions.prompt: Marzipan is a paste of sugar and which ground nut?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — marzipan is a confection of ground almonds and sugar.

questions.prompt: In 'Pulp Fiction,' what do Paris menus call the Quarter Pounder with Cheese?
questions.answer_note: source: Pulp Fiction (1994) — the metric system renames the Quarter Pounder a Royale with Cheese.

questions.prompt: Cognac is a brandy distilled from which fruit?
questions.answer_note: source: Cognac AOC rules — cognac is distilled from white wine grapes, chiefly ugni blanc; apple brandy is calvados.

questions.prompt: How many gallons of beer are in a standard full US beer barrel?
questions.answer_note: source: US Tax and Trade Bureau — a US beer barrel is defined as 31 gallons; a typical half-barrel keg holds 15.5.

questions.prompt: Sake is brewed mainly from what ingredient?
questions.answer_note: source: Japan Sake and Shochu Makers Association — sake is brewed from polished rice, water, koji, and yeast.

questions.prompt: Classic kimchi is most often made from which vegetable?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — baechu (napa cabbage) kimchi is Korea's most common variety.

questions.prompt: Which chef brought French cooking to American TV with 'The French Chef' in 1963?
questions.answer_note: source: PBS/WGBH — Julia Child's 'The French Chef' debuted on Boston public TV in 1963.

questions.prompt: Poutine — fries, gravy, and cheese curds — was born in which Canadian province?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — poutine emerged in rural Quebec in the late 1950s.

questions.prompt: Cheddar cheese is named after a village in England.
questions.answer_note: source: Oxford Companion to Cheese — cheddar originated around the village of Cheddar in Somerset, England.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of Escoffier's 5 French mother sauces?
questions.answer_note: source: Escoffier's Guide Culinaire — the 5 mother sauces are béchamel, velouté, espagnole, hollandaise, and tomato.

questions.prompt: By law, Scotch whisky must mature in oak casks for at least how many years?
questions.answer_note: source: Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009 — minimum maturation is 3 years in oak casks in Scotland.

questions.prompt: Traditional Worcestershire sauce gets its savory depth from which cured fish?
questions.answer_note: source: Lea & Perrins ingredients — Worcestershire sauce is fermented with anchovies, vinegar, and spices.

questions.prompt: Which fortified wine takes its English name from Jerez, the Spanish city where it is made?
questions.answer_note: source: Consejo Regulador del Jerez — sherry is the anglicized name of Jerez de la Frontera's fortified wine.

questions.prompt: Angostura bitters, in the famous oversized-label bottle, are made in which Caribbean nation?
questions.answer_note: source: House of Angostura — the bitters have been produced in Trinidad since 1875.

questions.prompt: In 'The Godfather,' Clemenza famously says to leave the gun and take which dessert?
questions.answer_note: source: The Godfather (1972) — Clemenza's cannoli instruction is one of film's most quoted food lines.

questions.prompt: Most rosé wine gets its pink color from brief contact with what?
questions.answer_note: source: Oxford Companion to Wine — rosé is made by short maceration of juice on red grape skins.

questions.prompt: Botanically, a strawberry is a true berry.
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — strawberries are accessory fruits; bananas actually are true berries.

questions.prompt: Arabica coffee is native to the highlands of which country?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Coffea arabica is indigenous to the highlands of Ethiopia.

questions.prompt: Sriracha sauce is named after a seaside town in which country?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — sriracha takes its name from Si Racha in Chonburi province, Thailand.

questions.prompt: Searing steak browns it through which reaction between amino acids and sugars?
questions.answer_note: source: Harold McGee, On Food and Cooking — Maillard browning requires amino acids plus reducing sugars.

questions.prompt: A martini garnished with a pickled cocktail onion goes by what name?
questions.answer_note: source: Oxford Companion to Spirits & Cocktails — a Gibson is a martini garnished with a cocktail onion.

questions.prompt: Traders from which country introduced the frying technique behind tempura to Japan in the 1500s?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Portuguese traders and missionaries brought the batter-frying technique to Japan in the 16th century.

questions.prompt: Which grape variety is the backbone of Chianti?
questions.answer_note: source: Chianti DOCG rules — Chianti must be at least 70% sangiovese.

questions.prompt: Green Chartreuse liqueur is still made by monks of which religious order?
questions.answer_note: source: Chartreuse distillery — Carthusian monks of the Grande Chartreuse make it from a 1605 manuscript recipe.

questions.prompt: Pharmacist John Pemberton created Coca-Cola in 1886 in which US city?
questions.answer_note: source: The Coca-Cola Company — Pemberton first sold the drink at an Atlanta pharmacy in 1886.

questions.prompt: Which chef's 2000 memoir 'Kitchen Confidential' spilled professional kitchen secrets?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Anthony Bourdain published 'Kitchen Confidential' in 2000.

questions.prompt: Sweet, sour, salty, bitter — what is the 5th basic taste called?
questions.answer_note: source: Umami Information Center — Kikunae Ikeda identified umami as the 5th basic taste in 1908.

questions.prompt: White chocolate contains cocoa butter but lacks which component of regular chocolate?
questions.answer_note: source: FDA standard of identity — white chocolate is cocoa butter, milk, and sugar with no nonfat cocoa solids.

questions.prompt: Hawaiian pizza was invented in Canada.
questions.answer_note: source: BBC obituary of Sam Panopoulos — he first put pineapple on pizza in Chatham, Ontario, in 1962.

questions.prompt: Kiwifruit was rebranded and exported by New Zealand, but the plant is native to which country?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — the kiwifruit vine is native to China and was long called the Chinese gooseberry.

questions.prompt: Prohibition ended in the United States in what year?
questions.answer_note: source: US Constitution, 21st Amendment — ratified December 5, 1933, repealing Prohibition.

questions.prompt: German chocolate cake is named after what?
questions.answer_note: source: Baker's Chocolate history — Samuel German created the namesake sweet baking chocolate in 1852.

questions.prompt: Cappuccino takes its name from the hooded robes of which order of friars?
questions.answer_note: source: Oxford English Dictionary — cappuccino refers to the brown hooded robes of Capuchin friars.

questions.prompt: Bond's Vesper martini in 'Casino Royale' calls for gin, vodka, and which French aperitif?
questions.answer_note: source: Ian Fleming's Casino Royale (1953) — the Vesper mixes gin, vodka, and Kina Lillet.

questions.prompt: Caesar salad was created in 1924 at Caesar Cardini's restaurant in which country?
questions.answer_note: source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — restaurateur Caesar Cardini created the salad in Tijuana, Mexico, in 1924.
